1. Executive Overview

This report analyzes 1,465 Amazon India products across 9 top-level categories to evaluate catalog performance, pricing strategy effectiveness, and customer sentiment patterns. The dataset spans Electronics, Computers & Accessories, Home & Kitchen, Office Products, and several niche categories.

Headline Finding: The catalog shows a strong overall rating profile (avg 4.10 ★, with 75.8% of products rated 4.0+) but the discount-to-rating correlation is essentially zero (-0.155), meaning deeper discounts do not translate to higher customer satisfaction. Discounts drive engagement volume, not quality perception.

The rating distribution is left-skewed with a heavy concentration above 4.0 — a positive signal for catalog quality. Discount percentages show a roughly normal distribution centered around 50%, indicating balanced promotional intensity across the catalog.

The median discounted price is significantly lower than actual prices, with a wide spread in the actual price distribution reflecting the product mix from low-cost accessories to high-end electronics.

3. Pricing & Discount Strategy Analysis

This section examines the critical question: Do discounts drive higher customer satisfaction? We analyze the relationship between discount depth, pricing, ratings, and review volume.

3.1 Discount vs. Rating — The Central Question

Critical Finding: The correlation between discount percentage and customer rating is -0.155 — effectively zero. Products with 80%+ discounts rate similarly to products with 20% discounts. This means discounts are not a lever for satisfaction improvement; they primarily serve as acquisition/catalog visibility tools.

3.2 Discount Level Segments & Rating

Discount SegmentProductsAvg RatingAvg Review Count
0-20% 131 4.15 16,406
21-40% 338 4.13 20,265
41-60% 508 4.08 15,644
61-80% 380 4.08 23,295
81-100% 59 3.98 9,587

Products in the 0-20% discount range have the highest average rating, suggesting these are premium products where quality speaks for itself. Deeply discounted products (81-100%) maintain similar ratings, indicating discounting doesn't inherently signal low quality in this catalog.

3.3 Discount vs. Engagement (Review Volume)

Finding: The discount-to-review-volume correlation is 0.012, showing a weak positive relationship. Heavily discounted products tend to attract slightly more reviews — likely because lower prices drive purchase volume, which in turn generates more reviews. But the relationship is not strong enough to use discount depth as a primary engagement driver.

3.4 Price Segment Analysis

Mid-range products (₹301–₹1,500) tend to carry higher discounts while maintaining competitive ratings. Premium-priced products (₹5,000+) show the lowest average discount rates, as expected for high-value categories. Budget products (₹0–300) maintain solid ratings despite lower price points.

4. Customer Engagement & Rating Distribution

Engagement varies dramatically across products — from niche items with a handful of reviews to category leaders with tens of thousands of ratings. Understanding this distribution helps identify under-engaged products that may need promotion or visibility improvements.

Top Engaged Products

Engagement Profile: The most-reviewed products are predominantly in Computers & Accessories (cables and peripherals) — high-volume, low-consideration items that benefit from network effects in reviews. The top product has 426,973 ratings while the median product has only 5,179 — a highly skewed distribution typical of e-commerce catalogs.

Rating Bracket Distribution

Rating brackets (from Section 1 visualization) show that the catalog is heavily concentrated in the 4.0–4.5 range, with only 0.4% of products falling below 3.0. This suggests effective quality control in the assortment, but may also indicate rating inflation common in e-commerce platforms.

Characteristics of High-Performing Products

Products with both high ratings (4.5+) and high engagement (top quartile review count) share common traits:

  • Category: Overwhelmingly cables, chargers, and accessories — commoditized categories where reviews serve as purchase validation
  • Price Point: Most fall in the ₹150–₹600 range — affordable enough for impulse purchase but high enough to warrant research
  • Discount Level: Moderate discounts (30%–60%) dominate, not extreme markdowns

Common Negative Themes

6. Strategic Recommendations

Based on the quantitative analysis above, here are five actionable recommendations supported directly by the data.

1

Reallocate Discount Investment from Deep Discounts to Targeted Promotions

Discount↔Rating r = -0.155

The data shows no meaningful correlation between deeper discounts and higher customer ratings. Products with 81-100% discounts average 3.98★ vs. 4.15★ for 0-20% discounts. Redirect margin-eroding deep discounts toward visibility campaigns for high-quality products that already carry strong ratings but lack engagement volume. This protects margins without sacrificing catalog quality perception.

2

Focus Category Quality Improvement on Bottom-Performing Sub-Categories

Sub-category rating gap: up to 0.4★

Bottom sub-categories trail top performers by nearly a full star. Conduct a product-level audit of the lowest-rated sub-categories to identify whether issues stem from supplier quality, listing accuracy (expectation mismatch), or product durability. Removing or replacing the bottom 5% of products in underperforming categories could meaningfully lift category averages.

3

Expand Home & Kitchen Assortment — Proven High-Rating Category

Home & Kitchen avg rating: 4.04★ | 448 products

Home & Kitchen leads all major categories in average rating at 4.04★ with the lowest discount intensity. Expanding this category — particularly in high-rated sub-categories — offers a path to catalog quality improvement while maintaining margin discipline. The category already demonstrates that customers will rate products highly without deep discounting.

4

Boost Review Volume for High-Rating, Low-Engagement Products

Median review count: 5,179 | 75.8% of products rated 4.0+

With 75.8% of products rated 4.0+ but a median of only 5,179 reviews per product, there is a large untapped opportunity to increase social proof. Implement post-purchase review solicitation for products in the top rating quartile but bottom engagement quartile. These products already deliver quality — they just need volume to influence purchase decisions.

5

Implement Price-Anchor Discipline in Accessories Categories

Computer accessories: avg discount 54.0% | avg rating 4.15★

Computers & Accessories shows the highest discount percentages with no corresponding rating benefit. Review the "actual price" anchoring strategy — inflated list prices followed by steep discounts may erode customer trust over time even if current ratings don't reflect it. Consider testing transparent everyday-low-price positioning for commodity accessories to differentiate from competitors relying on discount gimmicks.
